stories.title: Argentine leader says oil firms working off Falklands face sanctions
stories.summary: Argentina's President Javier Milei has said he will sanction oil companies working off the Falklands as he reiterated the country's claim on the British overseas territory in the south-west Atlantic Ocean. In a national address, Milei said the "winds of change" favoured Argentina's claim to the Falklands, pointing to Washington's readiness to review its neutrality on the dispute. Milei said the Sea Lion oilfield, where a British and an Israeli firm are due to begin exploration work, was a "clear and present danger". More than 40 years after the armed conflict over the territory, the sovereignty of the archipelago remains hotly disputed between Britain and Argentina. BBC News is seeking comment from the UK government on Milei's statement. It reiterated this week that Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future". The Sea Lion oilfield contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil, and production is expected to begin in 2028. "If we do not act swiftly in a few months, they will have the material capacity to access the oil that lies underneath our sea – something that has never happened before," Milei said. It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands. In a 2013 referendum, residents of the islands voted overwhelmingly to remain a British overseas territory - with 99.8% voting in favour and just three voting against. When asked in an interview with GB News earlier on Thursday if the US would "come to the UK's aid" during a potential territorial dispute, Trump replied that Britain had "not been there to help me" with his country's war with Iran.

stories.title: Dodgers take Shohei Ohtani out of lineup amid concerns about health
stories.summary: Ohtani has been plagued by right biceps pain and left knee issues. The knee soreness has prevented him from pitching since July 3.

stories.title: Johor air quality hits unhealthy levels, while Sarawak records very unhealthy API readings
stories.summary: Three areas in Malaysia have recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings while 10 other areas are showing unhealthy levels. According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the three very unhealthy API readings are in Sarawak, where Kuching has a reading of 298, followed by Samarahan (297) and Sri Aman (248) as at 8.30am on Sept 4. Six areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Sarikei (180), Sibu (175), Mukah (170), Bintulu (159), Samalaju (152) and ILP Miri (137), while in Sabah, Sandakan has a reading of 152 and Politeknik Kota Kinabalu’s API reading is 118. Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings in Pasir Gudang at 110 and Segamat at 107. Elsewhere in the country, 45 locations such as those in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor and Terengganu are seeing moderate API level readings while 10 locations in Penang, Kedah and Kelantan are showing good API levels. API readings of between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.
